issues.what: Yunnan, Guizhou and Guangxi unowned for the end of 1916: the 1916 keyframe (March-July state) is checked after the July ledger gain and snaps them out, then the 1917 keyframe snaps them back

About 670 Ukrainian cells (Kyiv, Kharkiv, Poltava, Dnipro, Zaporizhzhya and parts of Chernihiv, Sumy, Zhytomyr) unowned at the end of 1918: the Soviet republic's March-April losses go to german-empire as owner and its 1918 keyframe releases them; the Ukrainian State governed them
Tuva (631 cells) unowned from April to the end of 1914: the Uryankhay republic's dissolution leaves its land with nobody until the Russian 1915 keyframe

Mosul vilayet (about 210 cells) plain Ottoman at the end of 1918 and unowned in 1919 after the Ottoman keyframe; British troops entered Mosul on 14 November 1918 after the armistice, sovereignty unsettled
Rwanda and Burundi (179 cells) flip from Belgian-held Ruanda-Urundi to german-africa in 1918 through the German Africa keyframe, and to belgian-congo in 1919
About 250 cells of southern Mozambique held by portuguese-republic directly (dark green blob inside the colony) instead of portuguese-mozambique

About 2,000 cells of Angola (south-east, Moxico, Lunda, Huila) held by portuguese-republic directly, drawn in the Republic's own colour inside the colony. A trial patch (gains by portuguese-angola) was undone by the colony's own 1912 and 1915 keyframes, which release cells outside their shape, and made 1915 worse, so it was dropped

Congress Poland: the 1915 ledger hands the land to german-empire as owner, the German 1915 keyframe releases it, the Russian 1915 keyframe takes it back for one year-end and the 1916 keyframe releases it again: about 410 cells of Warsaw and Kielce unowned in 1916-1917, and Russian at the end of 1915; the German Government General of Warsaw (October 1915-1918) has no dossier

End of 1917 interregnum: the Russian Republic's dissolution passes only 'Russia' to the Soviet republic, so Belarus (785 cells), Transcaucasia (about 716), Estonia (228), Latvia (193), Moldova (129) and about 665 cells of Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan are unowned; Belarus stays unowned through 1918 (776 cells) and in part in 1919 (311)
